study_identification.title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

study_characteristics.study_objective: To determine whether cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in distinct neural cell types as inferred from gene expression data and person-specific genomic variation, and to validate cell-based patient subtypes using polygenic risk scores.

dataset_name.supporting_text: This study comprised a total of 1849 participants drawn from three independent datasets: (1) the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample [15]; (2) the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCPpsychosis) [16]; and (3) the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB) [17]. preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: T1-weighted images comprising the ASRB dataset were processed using FreeSurfer version 6 [4]. Processing and CTh estimation for the HCP-psychosis dataset followed the HCP1200 pipeline to facilitate harmonization of the HCP datasets. In brief, T1-weighted images for these datasets were processed using FreeSurfer version 5.3 [4]. For all three datasets, preprocessing included intensity normalization, nonbrain tissue removal and spatial normalization to Talairach-like space. Preprocessed images were segmented into gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, after which white matter and gray matter surfaces were reconstructed. CTh was estimated for each surface vertex based on the distance separating the gray and white matter surfaces and averaged over all vertices comprising each of the 68 cortical regions (34 per hemisphere) of the Desikan-Killiany atlas [5, 6].

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis:
Answer: For each patient, interregional correlation coefficients quantified spatial coupling between regional CTh deviation profiles (34 regions) and cell type-specific gene expression maps (7 cell types). Ansari-Bradley test evaluated whether observed correlations were more dispersed than null distribution (1000 permutations randomizing regional gene expression). Ward's linkage clustering with PCA dimensionality reduction identified three cell-based subtypes (gap statistic). Genomic validation: Partial correlations tested whether polygenic risk scores (PRS) constrained to cell type-specific genes covaried with whole-brain CTh deviation severity within corresponding subtypes, controlling for sex, genome-wide PRS, and familial relatedness. Validation results showed subtype-specific associations: Subtype I (neuronal/endothelial) r=-0.40, FDR p=0.010; Subtype III (astrocyte/OPC) r=-0.30, FDR p=0.028.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: The statistical analysis approaches are described in detail including the methods for relating CTh deviations to gene expression, clustering patients into subtypes, and validating subtypes with genetic data.
Supporting Text: Here, interregional levels of cell type-specific gene expression were correlated across the 34 cortical regions with individual deviations in regional CTh estimates (output from normative modeling; Fig. 1d). As the regional pattern of CTh deviations varied, we hypothesized that associations with specific cell types would only be evident in subsets of individuals. Therefore, the Ansari-Bradley test examined whether correlation distributions (across individuals) were more dispersed than a null distribution of correlation coefficients computed by randomizing the regional gene expression values (1000 permutations: Fig. 1d). ... For each dataset (i.e., Discovery and Validation), individuals with schizophrenia were classified into broad cell-based subtypes based on personspecific associations between their spatially patterned CTh deviation profile with interregional gene expression maps of specific cell types. To improve the clustering algorithm performance, dimensionality reduction with principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to the (subject x cell specific gene expression maps) correlation matrix, retaining a set of four principal components that captured the most variance, as described in [28]. Ward's linkage clustering algorithm was used to identify clusters of individuals based on the four principal components. The gap statistic was used to determine the optimal number of clusters (if any), ranging from 1-7. ... To validate cell-based patient subtypes, partial correlations assessed the degree to which polygenic cell type scores covary with severity in wholebrain CTh deviations in individuals comprising the corresponding subtype. Correlation analyses accounted for the potential confounding effects of sex, genome-wide liability for schizophrenia (sczPRS) and familial relatedness (see Supplementary Material for genetic computation of familial relatedness).

clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed:
Answer: In 1849 participants (discovery: 140 SZ, 1127 HC; validation: 335 SZ, 185 HC), quantile regression established age/sex-adjusted normative ranges for regional CTh. Most individuals with schizophrenia (>80%) fell within normative ranges per region, but showed more frequent infra-normal deviations in frontal, temporal, and insular cortices compared to controls. Across 34 cortical regions, individual CTh deviation profiles significantly covaried with interregional gene expression levels of five out of seven cell types: astrocytes, endothelial cells, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), excitatory neurons, and inhibitory neurons (Ansari-Bradley FDR<0.05). These associations were replicated in the independent validation cohort. Ward's clustering identified three cell-based subtypes: Subtype I (22% validation, 26% discovery) showed neuronal/endothelial-patterned thinning with widespread cortical involvement; Subtype II (43% validation, 27% discovery) showed weak cell-type associations with widespread thinning; Subtype III (25% validation, 47% discovery) showed astrocyte/OPC-patterned thinning with milder fronto-temporal involvement and preserved occipital CTh. Genomic validation in 231 ASRB patients demonstrated that polygenic risk scores constrained to cell type-specific genes covaried with CTh deviation severity in corresponding subtypes: neuronal/endothelial PRS with Subtype I (r=-0.40, FDR p=0.010); astrocyte/OPC PRS with Subtype III (r=-0.30, FDR p=0.028), with discriminant validity confirmed (non-significant correlations in non-matching subtypes).
Confidence Rating: High

For all cortical regions, more than 90% of the healthy individuals resided within the normative range, confirming the accuracy of the normative models. ... clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations:
Answer: Gene expression maps derived from neurotypical postmortem donors (not schizophrenia-affected); left hemisphere only; regional gene expression nonuniformity may reflect cell numbers and/or single-cell transcription levels (unclear); patterns not mapping neatly onto specific cell types may weaken polygenic prediction (mixed-cell subtype only nominally significant); cell type associations depend on gene set estimation source (human vs. mouse); no mechanistic interpretation possible from correlational data.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: The authors discuss several important limitations in the discussion section.
Supporting Text: Specifically, spatially resolved gene expression data derive from externally sourced healthy adult donors and thus, cannot precisely capture interregional expression patterns in the context of other individuals, particularly in a disease state. ... First, regional nonuniformity in cell type-specific gene expression may depend on cell numbers and/or single-cell transcription levels. While postmortem evidence across four species demonstrates that thicker regions contain more glial cells [32], nonuniformity in terms of gene regulation of specific cells remains unclear due to difficulties in measuring single-cell transcription levels. Second, patterns of CTh alterations that do not map neatly onto specific cell types may weaken the predictive power of polygenic risk. This may explain only nominally significant validation results in the mixed-cell subtype. Third, cell type associations with MRIderived phenotypes hinge on the estimation of cell type transcriptional maps. For example, Shin et al. [46] observed a positive correlation with transcriptional maps of neurons and microglia in healthy controls. This contrasts with our study, which observed a negative correlation with neuronal maps and no correlation with microglia in healthy controls. The major difference between Shin et al. [46] and our approach is the source data used to extrapolate gene sets.

general_notes.general_notes: This study demonstrates an innovative multi-scale approach linking genes, gene expression, and brain morphometry to understand CTh heterogeneity in schizophrenia. Gene expression data from Allen Human Brain Atlas (6 neurotypical postmortem brains, 5 males/1 female, ages 24-57 years) were aligned to 34 left hemisphere Desikan-Killiany regions. Seven cell types examined: astrocytes, endothelial, microglia, oligodendrocyte progenitors, excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons, and oligodendrocytes. Gene sets derived from single-cell studies of adult human cortex. Clinical characteristics: Discovery cohort illness duration 1.83±1.35 years, PANSS positive 13.75±4.98, negative 12.40±5.12; Validation cohort illness duration 15.74±9.83 years. Validation cohort sites: Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Brisbane, Newcastle. Discovery cohort sites: Brigham and Women's Hospital, Indiana Hospital, McLean Hospital. Supplementary analyses also examined surface area and gyrification deviations but main focus was cortical thickness. The study did not find demographic or clinical factors (age, sex, illness duration, IQ, positive/negative symptoms) that differentiated the three cell-based subtypes.
